newsitem.title: USA: CPC to spin off corn refining business.
newsitem.headline: CPC to spin off corn refining business.

text.p: CPC International Inc., maker of Hellmann's mayonnaise, Knorr soups and Mazola corn oil, said Wednesday it will spin off its corn refining business to shareholders as a new independent publicly owned company.

The new company will be the third-largest corn refiner worldwide, with businesses in 18 countries and sales of $1.5 billion in 1996, excluding non-consolidated joint ventures. It will also be the global leader in dextrose, a high value-added corn refining product, and in corn starch.

The business will include CPC's corn refining operations in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Asia, and Africa; stakes in a joint venture in Mexico and elsewhere; and licensing and technical agreements, chiefly in Asia and Africa.

The spin-off aims "to give both CPC and the new corn refining company the focus, flexibility, and resources they need for faster growth of sales, volumes, and profits," said C.R. Shoemate, CPC's chairman and chief executive.

After the spin-off, CPC will be a global branded packaged food company with its existing businesses in branded grocery products, baking, and foodservice. CPC's branded grocery products and foodservice businesses include Best Foods mayonnaise and Skippy peanut butter.

CPC's baking business makes and markets Thomas' English muffins and bagels; Entenmann's sweet baked products; Freihofer's, Oroweat, and Arnold breads and rolls; Boboli pizza crusts; and other premium fresh baked products.
Konrad Schlatter, currently senior vice president and chief financial officer of CPC International, will be chairman and chief executive of the new corn refining company.
Samuel Scott will continue as president and chief operating officer of the new company and will be responsible for the day-to-day operations of the business.

CPC, based in Englewood Cliffs, N.J., does not expect to assign any of its existing debt to the new company. It may launch an initial public offering of stock in the new company before distributing the new shares to existing shareholders.

The deal is expected to be completed by year's end, subject to approval of a definitive plan by CPC's board and receipt of a ruling by the Internal Revenue Service that it will be tax-free to CPC and shareholders.
CPC's stock rose $2.375 to $84.25 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
